title: Batch Parity & Encrypted-Queue Ergonomics

terminalSemantics.splitFixed: final-step-only; ZIP parts ordered by source page range; pages-0001-0010.pdf-style inner names
terminalSemantics.pageImages: final-step-only; PNG ZIP ordered by source page; page-0001.png-style inner names

nonBatchBoundaries: multi-input merge and visual page organization
acceptance: A complete standalone-to-Batch capability matrix marks each Quick task as recipe, terminal, or explicit boundary.
Extract/remove pages, flatten, sanitization, and target-size compression have deterministic reusable Batch semantics.
Batch recipe schema v4 explicitly migrates v2/v3 recipes without changing existing ordered step meaning.
Encrypted queue items request a per-file credential only after a protected-input failure and validate it locally before reuse.
Plaintext Batch credentials stay in page-owned memory only and never enter recipe JSON, project storage, diagnostics, filenames, or queue messages.
Output currentness depends on recipe fingerprint, input identity, and credential revision.
After PDF rewrites, Batch resolves the actual output encryption state before later steps consume the result.
Terminal split/page-image steps remain final and expose deterministic ZIP/result naming and ordering.
No executable-version or persistent 9/13/6 schema cut occurs in P16.
